issues.t: PCV valve cover failure causes oil burning and vacuum leaks
issues.sym: Rough idle, a whistle or hiss from the engine, blue exhaust smoke, oil use between changes, oil leaks, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation diaphragm built into the valve cover can tear, and a check valve in the intake manifold can fail. Pressure builds in the engine and oil gets pulled in and burned. GM addressed it in bulletin PIP5197J.
issues.next: Have a shop smoke-test for vacuum leaks and check the valve cover. Replacing the valve cover, and the intake manifold if needed, usually fixes it.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from water pump, housings and reservoir
issues.sym: Low coolant in the reservoir, a sweet antifreeze smell inside or outside the car, overheating, weak heat, or an A/C off due to high engine temperature message.
issues.why: Many plastic cooling parts on the 1.4 turbo crack or leak with age, including the thermostat housing, water outlet, reservoir and water pump. GM extended water pump coverage on many 2011-2014 cars under bulletin 14371A.
issues.next: Check coolant regularly and fix leaks quickly. Ask a dealer whether the water pump coverage applies to your VIN. Do not drive if the temperature gauge climbs, because overheating can ruin the engine.

issues.t: Loose negative battery cable causes warning messages
issues.sym: The dash display flickers or shuts off, and ABS, traction control or power steering messages pop up, sometimes with steering assist dropping out.
issues.why: The negative battery cable can develop a poor connection. GM issued bulletin 14311B and extended coverage to replace the cable.
issues.next: Ask a Chevrolet dealer whether the cable coverage applies to your VIN. Have the battery and cable connections tested if warnings come and go.

issues.t: Turbocharger underboost and wastegate problems
issues.sym: Weak acceleration, hesitation, a whining noise from the front of the engine, and a check engine light for low boost.
issues.why: The turbo's internal wastegate can stick or its seat can crack. Vacuum leaks from a failed PCV system or a loose charge pipe can cause the same symptoms.
issues.next: Have vacuum and boost leaks checked first, since those are simpler fixes. If the turbo itself is at fault, it usually needs to be replaced.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure and misfires
issues.sym: The engine shakes or stumbles, power drops, and the check engine light comes on or flashes.
issues.why: The ignition coil pack can corrode and fail over time, often together with worn spark plugs.
issues.next: Get the code read. Replace the faulty coil and any old spark plugs, and check the PCV system if misfires keep coming back.

issues.t: Timing belt must be replaced on schedule
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The engine suddenly quits while driving and then cranks but will not start.
issues.why: The 1.8L engine uses a rubber timing belt rather than a chain, and it is an interference design. If the belt breaks, the valves can hit the pistons.
issues.next: If there is no record of a belt, tensioner and idler change around the interval in the owner's manual, have it done now. If the engine dies and will not restart, have it towed rather than cranking it.

issues.t: 6T40 automatic hard shifting, loss of reverse or failure
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, no reverse gear, or the transmission failing outright.
issues.why: The 6T40 six-speed automatic in early Cruzes draws many complaints for hard shifting and internal failures. Leaking transmission cooler lines can also run it low on fluid.
issues.next: Check for fluid leaks at the cooler lines and have the fluid and codes checked. If it slips or loses reverse, limit driving and get it diagnosed before the damage spreads.

issues.t: Electric power steering sticks or feels notchy
issues.sym: Steering feels sticky or notchy near center, the car wanders at highway speed, or a service power steering message appears.
issues.why: The electric power steering rack can develop a stick-slip condition. GM issued special coverage bulletin 14232 for this on 2012 Cruzes.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Ask a Chevrolet dealer whether the coverage applies to your VIN. Also have the battery and negative cable checked, since a weak connection can cause similar steering warnings.

issues.t: Steering wheel or steering shaft not fully secured (recalls)
issues.sym: Play or looseness in the steering wheel, clunking in the steering, or the wheel not turning the car as expected.
issues.why: On some early cars the steering wheel was not properly fastened, and on others the bolt joining the steering shaft to the steering gear was not fully seated. Either could lead to loss of steering. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If the steering feels loose in any way, stop driving and have it towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Shifter may show Park when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car rolls after you shift to Park and shut it off, or the gear indicator does not match the gear.
issues.why: The shift linkage could be installed wrong at the factory, so the transmission might not be in Park even when the shifter says it is. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Always set the parking brake until the repair is done.

issues.t: Spilled oil can catch fire on the engine shield (recall)
issues.sym: Burning oil smell or smoke from under the car, especially after an oil change.
issues.why: Oil spilled during service could collect on the engine shield and ignite on hot parts. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Fuel tank strap brackets missing welds (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you would notice day to day. The risk shows up in a crash.
issues.why: Welds on the fuel tank strap brackets could be missing, so the tank might come loose and leak fuel in a crash. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and get the free repair done.

issues.t: Intermittent loss of power brake assist (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels hard and the car takes longer to stop, sometimes with a brake warning.
issues.why: The electric vacuum pump that helps power the brake booster might not switch on, cutting brake assist. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the VIN for open recalls. If the pedal turns hard, press much harder, stop safely and have it repaired before driving on.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy (recalls)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light may come on, though there can be no warning at all.
issues.why: A shorting bar in the driver's airbag connector could touch the terminals and stop the airbag from deploying in a crash. GM ran several recalls on this.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and get the repair done as soon as possible.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator may be the wrong part (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning beforehand.
issues.why: Some driver front airbags were built with an incorrect inflator part, so they could rupture or fail to inflate in a crash. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN right away and get the airbag replaced before driving more than you must.

issues.t: Right front axle shaft can break (recalls)
issues.sym: A clunk or bang from the front, then the engine revs but the car loses drive and may roll even in gear.
issues.why: The right front half shaft on some 1.4L turbo and manual transmission cars could fracture. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If you lose drive, set the parking brake and have the car towed.

issues.t: Engine block heater cord can crack in the cold (recall)
issues.sym: Cracked or split insulation on the block heater cord, exposed wires, or sparks when plugged in.
issues.why: The insulation on the block heater cord could crack in cold weather and expose the wires, creating a shock or fire risk. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and do not plug in the block heater until the cord is replaced.

issues.t: Shift cable can disconnect from the shifter (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter moves but the gear does not change, or the car is in a different gear than the indicator shows.
issues.why: The shift cable adjuster could come loose from the shift lever. The car might not be in Park when parked. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Always use the parking brake until the repair is done.

issues.t: Inner tie rod may separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, steering that wanders, or the steering wheel not lining up with the wheels.
issues.why: An inner tie rod might not have been tightened properly and could come apart from the steering gear, causing loss of steering. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If the steering feels loose or clunks, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Roof-rail side airbag inflator may rupture (recalls)
issues.sym: Usually no warning beforehand.
issues.why: The side curtain airbag inflators in the roof rail could rupture at a weld when they deploy and throw metal pieces. GM ran several recalls on this.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and get the repair done as soon as parts are available.

issues.t: Parking brake may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: The car creeps or rolls with the parking brake set, or the rear brakes make a clunk or rattle.
issues.why: Bolts on the rear parking brake bracket could back out, so the parking brake might not hold. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Park in gear or in Park on flat ground until it is fixed.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: You can pull the key out of the ignition even though the shifter is not in Park.
issues.why: A faulty park lock lever or key cylinder housing could let the key come out with the transmission not in Park, so the car could roll away. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Always confirm the car is in Park and set the parking brake before getting out.

issues.t: Clogged PCV passage causes oil leaks and code P1101
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P1101, oil seeping from seals and gaskets, and sometimes an oil smell through the vents.
issues.why: A plugged crankcase ventilation passage in the camshaft cover lets pressure build inside the engine and push oil out. GM covers this in bulletin 20-NA-047.
issues.next: Have a dealer or shop check the cover against bulletin 20-NA-047 and fix the ventilation problem before replacing leaking gaskets.

issues.t: Power loss in cold weather from icing intercooler
issues.sym: In cold weather the car hesitates, loses power, may stall, and can set a low boost code.
issues.why: Moisture can freeze inside the charge air cooler and block air going to the engine. GM addresses it in bulletin 22-NA-007, which may include a software update.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletin 22-NA-007. Drive gently until the engine warms up if you notice hesitation.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from hoses and expansion tank
issues.sym: Coolant level drops, a sweet smell, drips under the front, and overheating warnings.
issues.why: The newer 1.4 turbo still has leak-prone cooling parts, including hose flanges, the heater hose and the expansion tank.
issues.next: Check coolant regularly and find leaks early. Do not drive if the engine overheats.

issues.t: Cracked pistons
issues.sym: Rough idle, knocking, misfires, a check engine light or StabiliTrak message, and in bad cases sudden engine failure.
issues.why: Owners of second-generation 1.4 turbo engines report pistons cracking, often at fairly low mileage. Abnormal combustion under load is a suspected cause.
issues.next: If you hear knocking or get a misfire with a flashing check engine light, stop driving and have a compression or leak-down test done. Using the fuel grade the owner's manual recommends may help.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper piston can reduce braking (recall)
issues.sym: Longer stopping distances or a brake pedal that feels less firm.
issues.why: A coating on the rear brake caliper pistons could let gas pockets form, which reduces rear braking. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If braking feels weak, stop driving and have it inspected.

issues.t: Start/stop accumulator cover may leak fluid (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid leaking, odd shifting, or the car losing drive.
issues.why: Bolts on the start/stop accumulator end cap in the transmission could be missing or loose, letting fluid leak out and causing loss of drive. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If you see red fluid under the car or it loses drive, stop driving and have it towed.
